cells.tense: You are close to someone and still know which feelings are yours.
cells.ask: Offer one honest thing to someone today, then leave the response in their hands.
cells.core: You can feel what someone else is feeling without it taking over the room. That is not a small thing. The pull toward what matters to you stays lit even when you are standing close to another person — the closeness does not erase your direction. When you see yourself in someone, the line around your own life stays where it is. That recognition keeps working, whether or not anyone says it out loud.\n\nWhat this can carry next is weight. Not the stiff kind — the kind that holds under pressure without turning hard. You can carry something for someone without becoming a wall about it. Keeping this costs something: you keep choosing the other person, again, when merging would be easier and walking away would be simpler. The same thing that lets you feel with them is the one that holds you steady while you do it.
cells.sheetLine: You feel with people and still know where you end.
cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want

cells.tense: You are living inside a version of this closeness that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Let one unfinished thing with someone be finished today, and do not open it again.
cells.core: You are feeling other people's moods before they arrive. Somewhere ahead is a version where the two of you are aligned and understood, and you are already there — taking on what the other person might need before they have said a word. The pull toward what you actually want gets hard to find when so much of what fills the room belongs to someone else. Where they stop and you start is no longer clear, and the closeness you wanted has begun to cost you the thing you were close for.\n\nWhat closes this is not caring less. It is letting one thing have a real finish — no revival, no last word. What ends cleanly makes room for what comes next. One thing stops today, and you find out you are still here.
cells.sheetLine: You feel people's moods before they arrive.
cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want

cells.tense: You stopped moving toward people and kept the surface polite instead.
cells.ask: Ask one person one real question and stay past their first answer.
cells.core: The connection is not gone. You are just not moving toward it. You learned to keep relationships at the depth where nothing can be lost — friendly, useful, unentered. The pull toward what you actually want is still there too, but you are not steering by it. Everything stays on the surface and you call that being fine.\n\nWhat comes back first is not a feeling. It is one small adjustment: a conversation, a question that goes past the easy answer, a moment where you stay in the room after the surface runs out. You do not have to manufacture warmth — staying there long enough for the warmth you already have to show is the whole move. That is what changed the last time, and what shifts it now.
cells.sheetLine: You kept relationships where nothing can be lost.
cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want

cells.tense: You are already giving people something real and calling it nothing.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you actually notice about them, and stop there.
cells.core: People come to you and leave steadier. You would say you were just being practical, just listening, just there. But what they felt was not logistics — it was you, in contact with them, seeing them as they are. That happens whether or not you claim it. The pull toward what matters is shaping your choices too, though you would call those choices obvious.\n\nWhat is missing is not the caring. It is you standing behind it. You keep handing people the effect and keeping your name off it, as if saying so would make it less true. One plain sentence about what you see in someone would put the thing back where it belongs. You are the one doing this. That is not a compliment. It is a fact about where the pen is.
cells.sheetLine: You give people something real and call it nothing.
cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want
